ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in $\odot O$, with $AD\parallel BC$. $BD$ bisects $\angle ABC$, and $\angle A=126^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle BDC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AD \parallel BC$ and $\angle A=126^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle ABC=180^\circ-\angle A=180^\circ-126^\circ=54^\circ$,\\
Given that $BD$ bisects $\angle ABC$,\\
we have $\angle DBC=54^\circ\div 2=27^\circ$,\\
Since $AD \parallel BC$,\\
it follows that $\angle ADB=\angle DBC=27^\circ$,\\
Given that quadrilateral $ABCD$ is circumscribed around circle $O$,\\
it follows that $\angle ADC=180^\circ-54^\circ=126^\circ$,\\
Therefore, $\angle BDC=\angle ADC-\angle ADB=126^\circ-27^\circ=\boxed{99^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in $\odot O$, with $AD\parallel BC$. $BD$ bisects $\angle ABC$, and $\angle A=126^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle BDC$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Since $AD \parallel BC$ and $\angle A=126^\circ$,\\ it follows that $\angle ABC=180^\circ-\angle A=180^\circ-126^\circ=54^\circ$,\\ Given that $BD$ bisects $\angle ABC$,\\ we have $\angle DBC=54^\circ\div 2=27^\circ$,\\ Since $AD \parallel BC$,\\ it follows that $\angle ADB=\angle DBC=27^\circ$,\\ Given that quadrilateral $ABCD$ is circumscribed around circle $O$,\\ it follows that $\angle ADC=180^\circ-54^\circ=126^\circ$,\\ Therefore, $\angle BDC=\angle ADC-\angle ADB=126^\circ-27^\circ=\boxed{99^\circ}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: There is a circle in the figure, and the four points A, B, C, and D are on the circle, forming the cyclic quadrilateral ABCD in order. AD is the upper chord, BC is the lower chord, and the figure shows that AD is parallel to BC; the diagonal BD is drawn from B to D. The required angle ∠BDC is the angle at point D, formed by DB and DC.

Reasoning: It is known that AD ∥ BC, and ∠A = ∠DAB = 126°. Taking AB as a transversal, the interior angles on the same side are supplementary, so ∠ABC = 180° − 126° = 54°. Also because BD bisects ∠ABC, ∠DBC = 54° ÷ 2 = 27°. Since ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary, therefore ∠BCD = 180° − ∠DAB = 180° − 126° = 54°. In triangle BDC, ∠BDC = 180° − ∠DBC − ∠BCD = 180° − 27° − 54° = 99°.
